title: e2e-latency-profiling-traces-2026-04-18
content:
Executive summary:

This doc collects end-to-end latency profiling traces captured from the serving runtime for the 2026-04-17 nightly perf run targeting the 70B model family. The goal is to produce a reproducible per-stage breakdown (p50/p95/p99) and surface likely bottlenecks for follow-up investigation and remediation.

Quick conclusions (short):
- Overall p50: 180 ms, p95: 480 ms, p99: 920 ms for typical 32-token generation workload (prompt length 64).
- Biggest contributors at p95/p99: kernel execution variability (GPU queuing + occasional long kernels), model setup (initial KV warmup on cold workers), and network serialization spikes from large token-batched requests.
- KV cache miss rates correlate with the worst tail latencies; when prefix matches are low, p99 jumps ~2x.

Test configuration:
- Build: serving-runtime v3.7.1 + kernel-optimizer v1.12.
- Hardware: Dedicated cluster: 8x A100-80GB, 64GB host RAM, 100Gbps NICs.
- Orchestration: pod-per-hotspot (conservative packing), autoscaler disabled for run.
- Workload: synthetic traffic using loadgen v2.4. Scenario: 200 RPS steady, 32 token generation, temperature 0.2, top_p 0.95. Prompt length distribution: 20% short (16), 60% medium (64), 20% long (256).
- Model variant: rw-70b-qat-q4f16 (quantized), KV-cache on by default.
- Duration: 2 hours (steady-state window analyzed: 30-90 minutes).

Data collected:
- Per-request trace with stages: ingress, routing, model-setup, kv-lookup, kernel-exec, token-serialize, network-egress.
- Aggregates: p50/p95/p99 per stage, overall latency histograms, KV cache hit/miss markers, GPU occupancy snapshots, CPU-side RPC wait samples.

Overall latency (steady-state window):
- p50 overall: 180 ms
- p95 overall: 480 ms
- p99 overall: 920 ms
- Mean: 235 ms

Per-stage median and tails (values in ms):
- Ingress (LB + auth): p50 8, p95 25, p99 60
- Routing (policy eval + model selection): p50 12, p95 40, p99 90
- Model-setup (warmup, tensor load when cold): p50 15, p95 110, p99 260
- KV-lookup (prefix retrieval and cache check): p50 6, p95 45, p99 180
- Kernel-exec (GPU execution per token batch): p50 110, p95 235, p99 380
- Token-serialize (host-side I/O + proto encode): p50 18, p95 30, p99 50
- Network-egress (transport to client): p50 11, p95 15, p99 40

Observations and interpretation:
1) Kernel-exec dominates p50 and p95, but model-setup and KV-lookup dominate p99:
   - Kernel-exec is relatively stable at the median but shows a long tail due to occasional kernel scheduling spikes and larger sequence-length batches. GPU occupancy logs show ~85% for median windows but frequent short dips correlating to high p99 samples.
   - Model-setup has a modest median but very high p95/p99. Investigation shows these correspond to requests routed to recently launched pods where KV cache and compilation paths are not warmed.
   - KV-lookup p99 (180 ms) is alarming: traces show backend storage (redis-like) experiencing slow RPCs under bursty access patterns. When KV-cache hit rates exceeded 92% the p99 drops significantly.

2) Correlation with request attributes:
   - Long prompts (256) contribute disproportionately to kernel-exec tail; sequences >128 tokens increase kernel p99 by ~40%.
   - Mixed-batching (different sequence lengths) increases kernel variance; coalesced batches with high variance cause slower large-kernel runs.

3) Network/serialization spikes:
   - A subset of high-latency traces shows token-serialize + egress stacked to ~80ms due to a slow proto encode on older CPU instance types. Most occurrences are on specific nodes (node labels: legacy-cpu=high).

Reproducible trace examples (compressed summaries):
- Trace A (p50): ingress 6, routing 10, setup 12, kv 5 (hit), kernel 95, serialize 18, egress 10 => total 156 ms
- Trace B (p95): ingress 22, routing 35, setup 80, kv 30 (miss-ish), kernel 210, serialize 25, egress 15 => total 417 ms
- Trace C (p99): ingress 55, routing 90, setup 240 (cold pod), kv 170 (miss + backend delay), kernel 360, serialize 40, egress 50 => total 965 ms

Root causes (hypotheses):
- Cold pod/model-setup paths are not sufficiently amortized by our current pre-warming policy. New pods see high model-setup latency (tensor load + compilation) and cause severe tails.
- KV backend (external store) occasionally sees slow RPCs under bursty access leading to large KV-lookup tails. Timeouts/retries amplify latency.
- Kernel scheduling and mixed-sequence batching increase variance; our batching policy does not yet prioritize sequence-length homogeneity.
- A small number of legacy CPU nodes run slower proto encoders, contributing to serialization tail.

Immediate remediation ideas (short-term):
- Enforce stronger pre-warm: keep N idle pre-warmed pods per model family during peak windows. Measure cost tradeoff.
- Implement a cheap in-memory KV L1 cache co-located with worker to absorb short-term spikes (TTL ~30s) and reduce backend pressure.
- Adjust batching policy to prefer homogeneous sequence lengths within batches; add jitter to arrival times to reduce pathological coalescing.
- Avoid routing to legacy-cpu nodes for latency-sensitive models (node affinity override until proto encoder patched).

Suggested experiments (next runs):
1) Pre-warm test: run identical workload with "prewarm_count" set to 3 and 6 vs baseline 0. Compare p99 and model-setup stage distribution.
2) KV L1 pilot: enable local LRU cache on subset of nodes and measure KV backend RPC QPS and p99.
3) Batching policy variants: simulate homogenous-batching vs current policy to quantify kernel-exec tail reduction.
4) Node exclusion: exclude legacy-cpu nodes and measure token-serialize stage impact.

Action items (owners):
- Aisha: create JIRA tasks for pre-warm policy change and bench plan (JIRA-INF-790).
- Marco: instrument KV client with detailed per-RPC timing and add histograms (github PR planned).
- Chen: prototype L1 in-memory cache on worker runtime and run canary (branch runtime/l1-cache).
- Sofia: run controlled experiments for batching policy permutations and summarize results next week.

Notes / open questions:
- What is the cost impact of keeping N pre-warmed pods? Need finance estimate for 24/7 vs peak windows.
- Are we seeing any model-variant specific kernel regressions? Kernels optimizer team to check recent upstream kernel changes around v1.12.
- Checkpoint: reconcile these traces with prod observability (console traces) to ensure this reproduces in hosted mode.

Notes to self (informal):

- reach out to kernels team re: any changes around kernel scheduling heuristics in v1.12.
